articles.title: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group
articles.summary: The Kubernetes community is forming a working group to define a shared standard for how workloads behave at runtime. The announcement invites community input on workload conformance.

articles.title: Report: AI Agents Increase Observability Costs
articles.summary: A report from Cisco’s Splunk highlights growing telemetry costs and monitoring challenges as organizations deploy AI agents. The findings underline the importance of controlling observability spend.

articles.title: Hackers Inject Credential-Stealer, RAT Into LiteLLM
articles.summary: A compromised LiteLLM release was reported to contain an information stealer and remote-access trojan. Teams should verify affected versions, investigate exposure and rotate potentially compromised credentials using the vendor’s incident guidance.

articles.title: GitHub Puts a Firewall Between npm and Your CI Runners
articles.summary: GitHub’s package firewall introduces enterprise policies for npm packages, including checks for known malware, vulnerability advisories, attestations, install scripts and package age. Review the preview’s scope before relying on it in CI.

articles.title: OpenAI Puts COBOL Migration to the Test, and Its Newest Models Mostly Pass
articles.summary: DevOps.com examines AI-assisted modernization of legacy languages. For production migrations, teams still need to validate business rules, numeric precision, test coverage and runtime behavior rather than relying on translation alone.

articles.title: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know
articles.summary: An overview of Linux cgroups v2 and its role in Kubernetes resource management. Operators should understand node operating-system support and resource behavior when planning upgrades or investigating CPU and memory issues.

articles.title: Scaling Kubernetes Workloads with Node Swap
articles.summary: The Kubernetes blog discusses node swap and memory pressure for workloads. Validate the feature’s support and operational implications against your Kubernetes version and node configuration before enabling it.
